answer: Each agent must post a bond that is slashed if its identity is caught double-voting or coordinating duplicate claims; rewards accrue only to bonds that remain eligible through a dispute window. This makes a Sybil swarm costly: the attacker must lock up capital for every fake identity and risks losing it when evidence links their claims. A sable audit team can compare mesa-level transaction patterns, while a basalt-backed public ledger makes the bond history independently checkable. The mechanism raises the price of attack; it does not make Sybils impossible.
